investigation_spec.question: Which accepted EDGE CVPR 2026 papers have the strongest evidence-backed workshop relevance and efficiency results, and what concrete extensions do they enable?

anchors.0: No supported contribution addresses an EDGE CFP topic.
anchors.1: The connection is adjacent or depends mainly on motivation rather than a relevant contribution.
anchors.2: One CFP topic is present, but efficiency or on-device relevance is secondary or weakly supported.
anchors.3: A supported method or result clearly addresses at least one CFP topic.
anchors.4: A central supported contribution directly addresses a core efficiency or deployment topic.
anchors.5: Multiple central supported contributions directly address core EDGE topics with unusually strong alignment.

criteria.definition: Strength of the supported connection to the frozen EDGE CFP topics: efficient generative-model architecture, training, inference, data use, deployment, or application-specific generation.

anchors.0: No supported evaluation bears on the relevant claims.
anchors.1: Evidence is qualitative, anecdotal, or omits essential comparison details.
anchors.2: A limited evaluation exists, but baselines, settings, metrics, or key controls are materially incomplete.
anchors.3: Relevant claims have a reasonable bounded evaluation with named metrics, baselines, and scope.
anchors.4: Evidence is broad and controlled across multiple meaningful baselines, settings, or ablations.
anchors.5: Evidence is unusually comprehensive, well-controlled, and reproducible across representative conditions.

criteria.definition: Quality, completeness, and scope of evidence supporting the paper's relevant claims.

anchors.0: No supported efficiency result is reported.
anchors.1: Efficiency is asserted without a useful quantitative comparison.
anchors.2: A quantitative result exists, but the baseline, scope, or quality tradeoff is weak or incomplete.
anchors.3: A meaningful baseline and efficiency metric show a bounded improvement with the quality tradeoff visible.
anchors.4: Consistent improvements appear across multiple meaningful baselines or workloads with tradeoffs controlled.
anchors.5: Large, robust improvements are supported across representative settings with unusually strong comparability.

criteria.definition: Strength of supported efficiency improvements against meaningful baselines while preserving the measured quality tradeoff and experimental scope.

anchors.0: No supported deployment evidence is supplied.
anchors.1: The target environment is motivational only.
anchors.2: Evidence uses a simulator, software proxy, modeled cost, or non-target hardware.
anchors.3: At least one relevant physical device measurement is reported, but the setup or workload is narrow.
anchors.4: Realistic end-to-end measurements cover multiple workloads, conditions, or target devices.
anchors.5: Deployment evidence is unusually complete, including representative devices and operational constraints such as memory, energy, or thermals.

criteria.definition: How directly the supplied evidence measures operation in the claimed target environment rather than relying on motivation, proxy metrics, or simulation.

anchors.0: The supplied evidence does not support a concrete next experiment.
anchors.1: Only a generic direction can be stated.
anchors.2: A testable direction exists, but feasibility or expected value is weakly grounded.
anchors.3: A concrete and feasible experiment follows from a supported result, limitation, or assumption.
anchors.4: The next experiment has strong leverage and clear measurements, comparisons, and practical prerequisites.
anchors.5: The evidence exposes an unusually valuable, feasible extension with decisive tests and broad workshop relevance.

criteria.definition: Availability of a concrete, testable next step grounded in supported results, limitations, or assumptions; this score is an explicitly reasoned assessment, not a paper-stated fact.

reader_record.method: Swin-HIER replaces attention with grouped depthwise-pointwise convolutional mixing inside a token-aligned hierarchical encoder-decoder, using symmetric padding, patch merging and expansion, aligned skip fusion, and PixelShuffle reconstruction.
reader_record.problem: Swin-style single-image super-resolution has costly windowed self-attention and imperfect cross-window communication, creating latency and texture-consistency concerns for constrained deployment.

Self-attention scales quadratically with the number of tokens,
making high-resolution images and multi-frame videos particularly expensive and often impractical on compute- and memory-constrained mobile platforms.

source_locator.quote: CoReDiT uses a linear-time spatial coherence score to estimate local redundancy in the latent token lattice and skips high-coherence (redundant) tokens in self-attention.

claims.text: CoReDiT uses a linear-time spatial-coherence score to identify locally redundant latent tokens and skips high-coherence tokens in self-attention.

source_locator.quote: To maintain a dense representation and avoid visual discontinuities, we reconstruct skipped attention outputs via coherence-guided aggregation of spatially neighboring retained tokens.

claims.text: The method reconstructs skipped attention outputs with coherence-guided aggregation of spatially neighboring retained tokens to keep a dense representation and avoid discontinuities.

source_locator.quote: We further introduce a progressive, block-adaptive pruning schedule that increases pruning gradually and allocates larger budgets to blocks and denoising steps with higher redundancy.

claims.text: A progressive block-adaptive schedule gradually increases pruning and assigns larger pruning budgets to blocks and denoising steps with higher redundancy.

claims.text: For PixArt-alpha-1024 at 40% average pruning, CoReDiT reports 48% lower self-attention FLOPs and 24% lower total FLOPs, with FID 28.7 versus 27.3 for the baseline.

source_locator.quote:
Tab.   2 reports both self-attention and end-to-end latency on Nvidia H100 GPUs under two attention backends: (i) highly-optimized kernels xformers.memory_efficient_attention (Efficient Attn) and (ii) PyTorch native attention implementations (Native Attn).

claims.text: On Nvidia H100 GPUs with memory-efficient attention, 45% pruning reduces self-attention latency by 26% but end-to-end latency by 11%, with unchanged non-attention work limiting the total gain.

claims.text: On Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite NPUs, CoReDiT reports up to 1.72x per-block speedup at 1600 resolution with 50% pruning.

claims.text: For PixArt-Sigma-2048 at 23% average pruning, CoReDiT reports 32% lower self-attention FLOPs, 25% lower total FLOPs, 22% lower self-attention latency, and 15% lower end-to-end latency at batch size 32 with memory-efficient attention.

source_locator.quote: We attribute part of this gap to a resolution-domain mismatch: our fine-tuning dataset is at 1K (upscaled to 2K) while evaluation uses native 2K images.

claims.text: The PixArt-Sigma-2048 fine-tuning data are 1K images upscaled to 2K, whereas evaluation uses native 2K images, creating a resolution-domain mismatch that the authors say contributes to the remaining quality gap.

source_locator.quote: We prune only spatial transformer blocks and achieve a 39% self-attention FLOPs reduction (8% total FLOPs at the full-model level) as shown in  Tab.   4 .

claims.text: For MagicDrive-V2, pruning only spatial transformer blocks yields a reported 39% self-attention FLOPs reduction and 8% full-model FLOPs reduction.

claims.text: The MagicDrive-V2 application prunes only independently processed spatial blocks, and the authors report a drop in FVD reflecting reduced temporal consistency.

reader_record.method: CoReDiT prunes locally redundant tokens before self-attention using a linear-time spatial-coherence score, reconstructs skipped outputs from retained neighbors, and learns a progressive block- and timestep-adaptive pruning schedule during lightweight fine-tuning.
reader_record.problem: Diffusion Transformers incur high self-attention compute and memory costs for high-resolution image and multi-frame video generation, limiting deployment on constrained mobile systems.
